name: Elishama
title: Scribe at the King's Court
summary: Elishama was a scribe (secretary) at the court of King Jehoiakim in Judah. He played a role in the events surrounding the scroll of the prophet Jeremiah, as he kept the scroll in his chamber. He is mentioned in the book of Jeremiah as one of the officials of the court during the final period of the kingdom of Judah before the exile.

keyEvents.title: The Scroll of Jeremiah Read to the Princes
keyEvents.description: After Baruch had read the words of Jeremiah to the people, the scroll was brought to the chamber of the princes where Elishama worked as a scribe.

keyEvents.title: The Scroll Kept with Elishama
keyEvents.description: The princes gave orders that the scroll should be placed in the chamber of the scribe Elishama for safekeeping before they went to inform the king.

keyEvents.title: The King Sends Jehudi to Retrieve the Scroll
keyEvents.description: King Jehoiakim sent Jehudi to fetch the scroll from the chamber of Elishama so that it could be read aloud to the king.

keyEvents.title: The Scroll Is Read to King Jehoiakim
keyEvents.description: The scroll was brought from the chamber of Elishama and read aloud to the king, who cut it into pieces and threw it into the fire as each section was read.

keyEvents.title: The Princes Attempt to Prevent the Destruction
keyEvents.description: Elishama was among the officials present during this critical period when God's word through Jeremiah was delivered to the leaders of Judah.
